description: We are a team of 4 working on the "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Excited to explore satellite data and build our solution!
summary: We believe science should be accessible to everyone. Our project offers a beginner-friendly platform for exploring global fire activity, starting with North America. Using a grid-based approach to unify MODIS and VIIRS data, users can explore regions, compare fire activity across time periods, and learn about local fires through an educational chatbot. Rather than replacing NASA's FIRMS, our platform makes its data more accessible and easier to understand.
details:
This project provides a unified calendar for global fire activities. Rather than replacing NASA's FIRMS, our platform aims to make FIRMS data more accessible and easier to understand for users ranging from researchers to general audiences, especially students.

We preprocess the data using Python and GeoPandas. Then, we store the data in Parquet files with Zstandard compression and query them using DuckDB. For web development, we use OpenLayers 10 with WebGLVectorLayer and a simple FastAPI backend. A local Ollama model, gemma4:e2b, powers the chatbot.

The creativity of this project lies in its feature for comparing summary statistics across different time ranges and its GitHub-style activity calendar. Throughout the brainstorming and development process, we strongly focus on making the platform beginner-friendly so FIRMS data can be accessible for everyone.
